name: Validation Harness & Evidence
purpose: Prove what the platform can and cannot claim. Owns the sprint-validation policy engine for the twelve SEC cards, the isolated test runner, the original-asset verifier, the comparative evaluation harness and every stored evidence artefact under deploy/validation.

public_interfaces.name: sprint validation policy engine
public_interfaces.contract: Every numbered card item carries exactly one verdict; PASS needs evidence, BLOCKED needs a named prerequisite, and a physical-site item can never be closed with demonstration evidence.

public_interfaces.name: isolated test runner
public_interfaces.contract: Runs the full unittest suite against a temporary data root so repository incidents and manifests are never overwritten.

public_interfaces.name: original asset verifier
public_interfaces.contract: Detects Git LFS pointer files and verifies restored media checksums; reports missing assets instead of assuming them.

public_interfaces.name: stored evidence set
public_interfaces.contract: Every claim in the documentation points at a reproducible command, an exit code and a stored artefact.

runtime_dependencies: the full runtime stack when the whole suite runs
acceptance_criteria: python scripts/run_tests.py executes the suite in an isolated temporary data root.
The policy engine rejects a PASS that lacks an evidence reference and rejects physical-site items closed with demo evidence.
verify_original_assets.py distinguishes pointers from real media.
deploy/VALIDATION.md is regenerated from evidence, never hand-edited into a claim.
risks: The harness needs the pinned runtime dependencies; it could not be executed in the decomposition sandbox, so its command is verified by inspection only.
A validation harness is only as honest as its evidence classes; the physical-site gate is the control that keeps the product from overclaiming.
